script.title: Chapter 27: The Last of the Old Houses

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The inner courtyard of the estate house at first light after the rains. The great jackfruit tree over its worn stone platform. Beneath the branches, a pyre of stacked mango wood. Mourners in white stand back at a distance, small figures. Leaning against the trunk, alone: the dead mistress's long walking stick. Padmini does not appear alive anywhere in this panel; no one holds or leans on the stick.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fever that followed the last rains took Padmini Amma in three days.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Quick and unsentimental, as she would have chosen.

panels.description: Four bearers carry a white-shrouded body on a bamboo bier around a ring of old stones set into the courtyard floor; the shroud covers the body entirely. Nagoji is the bearer nearest the camera, at the front, face turned toward us (Kerala topknot, no turban, only a touch of grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; bare-chested, plain white mundu with no border, shoulder cloth knotted at the waist; no coat, no chain, no sacred thread, no forehead marks; the old brand a small ridged scar on his inner left forearm, turned away from camera). The other three bearers are older, grey-haired house elders. A Hindu funeral priest (V13 temple priest face, sacred thread, ash marks on his forehead) walks ahead of the bier, lips moving.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: As her adopted son, some duties fell to me that no woman, however senior, could perform in the eyes of temple and custom.

panels.description: Tight. The priest's hand passes a burning torch; Nagoji's right hand, nails healed but ridged, closes around it. Firelight on the underside of his thick moustache, his clean-shaven chin and set jaw, the small gold ear stud catching it. His left forearm stays out of frame.

Medium. Nandini, a small girl of about six, both arms wrapped around a brass water pot so large it rests against her stomach. Beside her Revathi Bayi (a little younger than Nagoji, tali, grey threading at the temples; for the rites she wears plain white with no border, no jasmine, no gold except the tali), one hand on the child's shoulder. Behind them the house elders, shoulder cloths knotted tight. Nagoji is not in this panel.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her heir was her sister's girl, Nandini.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The elders asked Revathi and me to stand with the house until the child could carry the name herself.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The pyre alight. Smoke climbs through the jackfruit leaves into a pale sky. Nagoji small beside the flames, the burning torch lowered in his right hand (same funeral look as 1.2: topknot, a touch of grey, moustache, clean chin, bare-chested, plain white mundu; left forearm turned away). In the foreground, soft focus, the walking stick against the trunk.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She had scolded kings in the shade of that tree.

panels.description: Widescreen strip, top. Some months later. The verandah of the estate house, a low writing desk. Nandini scratches her mark on a palm leaf with an iron stylus, tongue between her teeth, Nagoji's hand guiding her small one. Beside her mark he signs with the stylus. Nagoji (Kerala topknot, no turban, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; white mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain of office; no coat, no knife, no bandage). A tax collector waits on the step with his palm-leaf bundle. Padmini does not appear.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not inherit that estate. No man truly does here.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My work was to keep the roof sound and the vines alive until she grew into her own temper.

panels.description: Wide. The war hall. A large hand-drawn map of the coast across a table, unlabelled: territories as ink washes and hatching only, red to the north, black to the northeast, brown to the east, and all along the sea tiny drawn hulls in blue; no writing anywhere on it. Travancore itself a narrow shape at the southern tip. Ramayyan Dalawa (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) sits at the table's end among palm-leaf bundles, stylus in hand. Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces) stands over the map. Across from him, Nagoji in uniform (Kerala topknot, no turban, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office; no knife, no bandage).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Mysore. The Nizam. Arcot.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And all around the coast, the Europeans, with the patient hunger of men who thought in generations.

panels.description: Tight. A hand in cream and gold, one finger tracing the border of the king's own small kingdom on the unlabelled map, very small against the inks pressing on it. No face in frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We are small. If even two of them agreed to split us, we would last a season.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Perhaps two.

panels.description: Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) looking up across the table at Nagoji (uniform look as 2.2: topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat), one open hand passing over the map.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do you know why I have spent twenty years taking every small kingdom on this coast?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: To deny them footholds.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Partly. A hundred small kingdoms are a hundred small throats to cut.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) closes his hand into a fist and sets it on the centre of the map, knuckles over the crowded inks. His face level and unheated, his eyes on Nagoji out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: One larger kingdom is a single throat, yes, but it is also a single fist.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I do not take these lands because I am greedy. Divided, we are meat. United, we are at least a problem.

panels.description: Wide. The war hall. Ramayyan Dalawa (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) sets his stylus down across a palm leaf, deliberately. Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) and Nagoji (uniform: topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain) turn toward him across the unlabelled map.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Kottarakkara.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The name fell into the room like a stone into water.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Yes. Kottarakkara. The last of the old houses that still believes it can stand alone.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji (Kerala topknot, no turban, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; white coat, red waistcoat), eyes lowered to the map, where a hand in cream and gold rests on a hill town ringed in ink. Ramayyan's stacked palm-leaf bundles soft at the panel edge. No other face in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had known this day was coming.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The foreshadowing had been there for years, in Revathi's silences, in Padmini's careful warnings, in the notes Ramayyan kept that I had glimpsed and pretended not to understand.

panels.description: Wide. A red laterite road winding up into green hills. A Travancore column on the march: Travancore musketeers (Nair men in white coats or white mundu with cross-belts and matchlocks; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats) in file, bullock carts behind. Nagoji (uniform: topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat; no turban) mounted on a dark horse at the column's side. On the far hill, the steep tiled roofs of an old palace.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Raja of Kottarakkara had finally pushed too far. Dutch factors in his court. Letters intercepted that spoke of alternatives.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When we marched, he fled to Kochi, leaving the throne empty. But his kinswoman remained.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Dusk, months on, outside the besieged hill town. A road blocked with felled palms. A canal dammed with packed earth. Merchant carts turned back by Travancore sentries (Nair men in white mundu with spears and matchlocks; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats) while supply carts roll the other way toward the siege lines. On a bund, two officers watch: Eustachius De Lannoy (a head taller, pale hair going grey, clean-shaven European face, plain white Travancore coat with no red waistcoat; NOT a Dutch blue coat) and Nagoji (a head shorter, dark topknot, grey at the temples, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, red waistcoat under a white coat, silver chain). On the hill beyond, the old palace, ringed by the first siege fires.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: This is not war. This is siege without walls.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Walls can be rebuilt. What we are breaking cannot.

panels.description: Widescreen strip. The war hall at a later sitting, lamps lit. In the foreground, Marthanda Varma's hand (cream and gold) holds a rolled palm-leaf letter, its cord cut, a red lac seal split cleanly in two. Above it his face (V13 face), lamplit, reading. Behind, the unlabelled map, the hill town now closed inside a full ring of ink.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then Savitri's letter came.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Under the matrilineal laws of her house, she was the senior woman of Kottarakkara.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She demanded recognition. She demanded Kottarakkara. She demanded what Marthanda Varma had already decided to keep.

panels.description: Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) turned half away from the table toward a shuttered window, the palm-leaf letter lowered at his side. Nagoji (uniform: topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat) watching him from across the map.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If I give her the throne of Kottarakkara, every house I have absorbed will see it as permission to demand the same.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They will point to Savitri and say, see, the old ways still hold.

panels.description: Over Marthanda Varma's shoulder (cream and gold, his profile in the foreground, eyes on nothing): Nagoji (topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat) level across the table.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if you refuse?

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Then I make an enemy of a woman with legitimate grievances and powerful friends. The Dutch will use her. And Velinadu...

panels.description: Night. The Velinadu verandah. Revathi Bayi alone (a little younger than Nagoji; indigo sari with gold, tali, flat-coin necklace, grey threading at the temples, jasmine in her braid) by a brass lamp, a tied palm-leaf letter unopened in her lap, looking at nothing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Velinadu was Revathi. And Revathi was blood kin to Savitri.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The war hall. Ramayyan Dalawa (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth), stylus back in his fingers, eyes on the leaf and not on the king. No other face in frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Did you know it would be her?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I knew it would be someone like her. Sharp. Legitimate. Connected.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The worst kind of enemy: one who is not wrong.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Dusk. The old palace on its hill: steep tiled roofs, its great gate braced shut, ringed below by Travancore siege fires. Up the path climbs a small party: Nagoji on foot (topknot, no turban, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat, sword sheathed), with two Nair guards in white mundu, one carrying a plain white cloth tied to a spear-shaft.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kottarakkara. Savitri.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Names that meant nothing to me when I first washed up on this coast, and everything now.

panels.description: Interior. A pillared hall of dark carved wood. Behind Nagoji, the great doors braced with timber beams, a small wicket gate in them standing open, a retainer holding it. Savitri's retainers (local men in plain mundus with spears; no uniforms) along the walls. At the far end, Savitri of Kottarakkara, straight-backed (about fifty, lean face, lines of care at the eyes and mouth, black hair streaked grey in a low knot at the nape, no jasmine, no jewellery, plain white mundu and neriyathu with no border). Nagoji (topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain) stands just inside the wicket, alone, sword sheathed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She held herself like someone who had spent a lifetime being told she could not, and had decided otherwise.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: The Maratha rider. Marthanda Varma's foreign sword.

panels.description: Savitri (white mourning, grey-streaked low knot, lined face, no jewellery) slowly circling Nagoji, looking him up and down. Nagoji (topknot, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat) stands still, his hands held away from his sword hilt.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am not here to fight you.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: No. You are here to measure me.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: To see if I am the kind of threat that can be bought, or frightened, or simply waited out.

panels.description: Savitri (white mourning, grey-streaked low knot, lined face) stopped square in front of Nagoji (topknot, moustache, clean chin, white coat), smiling, and there is no warmth in it. Nagoji level.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And which are you?

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: I am the kind that remembers.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Savitri close (lean lined face, grey-streaked hair in a low knot, plain white), her face hard in lamplight. Behind her, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: a shut door, a narrow barred window, a man's open hand flat against the wood. No face on the man.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: My kinsman died in a room he could not leave, asking for air, asking for home.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Your king calls that statecraft. I call it murder dressed in manners.

panels.description: One of Savitri's retainers (plain mundu) steps off the wall toward Nagoji, reaching for his sheathed sword; Savitri (white mourning, grey-streaked low knot, lined face, no jewellery) stops him with one raised hand without looking at him. Nagoji (topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat) holds his ground, hands at his sides.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He threatened Travancore's unity. He invited our enemies into his court.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: He defended his house. As his mothers did before him. As I will.

panels.description: She steps in close. Tight two-shot: Nagoji (topknot, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat) and Savitri (lean lined face, grey-streaked low knot, plain white mundu and neriyathu), her eyes on his.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Do you know why your king fears the matrilineal law?

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Not because it is old. Because it gives women like me standing.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: A claim that does not depend on which man thinks he owns me.

panels.description: Savitri (plain white, grey-streaked low knot) at the doorway of the house shrine, her back half to camera, drawing up the wick of a tall brass lamp with her fingertips as she speaks. Its flame steadies and brightens.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Your king builds a state where power flows downward from one throne.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: We come from a world where it flows sideways. Through sisters, through daughters, through the women who remember.

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons) seen through the shrine doorway, the lamp flame large and out of focus in the foreground, its glow on his brass buttons. He is quiet.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That world is ending.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI (off)
copy.text: Perhaps. Or perhaps it will outlast his walls.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Low angle. Savitri (lean lined face, grey-streaked low knot, plain white) facing him fully, the lamp flame behind her head.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Empires fall. Women remain.

panels.description: Savitri (plain white, grey-streaked low knot) at a window, her back to Nagoji, looking out over the ring of Travancore siege fires on the plain below. Nagoji (topknot, white coat, red waistcoat) behind her, soft focus.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Tell him I will not disappear quietly. Tell him the Dutch have already made offers.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You would sell your coast to the very powers you claim to oppose?

panels.description: Savitri alone, in profile (lean lined face, grey-streaked hair in a low knot, plain white), against the siege fires beyond the window.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: I would survive. We outlast the men who think they own us.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: We tend our gardens long after their forts have fallen.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. A field of trampled paddy under drifting smoke, a small roadside shrine half hidden in the palms. Across it, Savitri sits a horse (lean lined face, grey-streaked low knot; her white mundu and neriyathu grey with dust and smoke), a sword at her side. Behind her, her force: local retainers in mundus carrying Dutch flintlocks and spears, no uniforms, under a plain cloth banner with a painted emblem and no script. In the foreground, Travancore musketeers (Nair men in white coats or white mundu with cross-belts and matchlocks; NOT blue coats, NOT red coats), and at the panel edge Nagoji's shoulder in a white coat and the back of his dark topknot. No blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When the palace could no longer hold, she went to the Dutch. They armed her cause.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was house land, temple land. Men fought not just for pay or king, but for the idea that the old names still meant something.

panels.description: Tight, across the field. Savitri's eyes (lean lined face, grey-streaked hair, dust on her white clothes) finding his through the dust.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She did not look like a villain. She looked like a woman who had weighed her choices and found them all bitter.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Evening. The field emptied. Spears in the mud, the plain cloth banner trodden down, an abandoned flintlock. Far off, small figures of Dutch factors in dark civilian coats hurry west along a canal road into the palms. No shore or sea in frame. No bodies, no blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We won. Not because we were right, but because we had more.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: More guns. More discipline. More of the terrible arithmetic that decides such things.

panels.description: Wide. Sunset through the open flap of the king's tent at the edge of the field. Nair guards (white mundu, spears) bring Savitri in: hands bound in front of her with cord, a bruise darkening one cheekbone, her white clothes grey with dust, grey-streaked hair in a low knot. She stands straight. Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold, a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest) seated, his spear leaning on the tent pole. Nagoji (topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, white coat with dust on it, red waistcoat) standing to one side.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Savitri herself was captured trying to reach the coast.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You could have run.

panels.description: Savitri (lean lined face, bruised cheekbone, grey-streaked low knot, bound hands), chin up.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: This is my land. I will not watch it from a ship.

panels.description: Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) has risen and crossed the tent. Varma and Savitri (plain white, bound hands, bruised cheekbone) face each other at arm's length. The guards look at the ground. Hold it.
Marthanda Varma close (V13 face, cream and gold), the weight of years in his face. At the panel edge, Savitri's profile (lined face, grey-streaked low knot), her reaction just beginning.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I met you once. When we were young. Before any of this.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You had a laugh that carried across courtyards.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) and Savitri (plain white mourning, bound hands, grey-streaked low knot) in profile, close, facing each other; Nagoji not in frame. Something flickers in her face and is put away.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: I have not laughed in a long time.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: No. Neither have I.

panels.description: Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) half-turned toward the tent flap, looking back at her over his shoulder: the king again.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I will not kill you. I will not imprison you.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You will go to Kochi, to the Dutch who promised you so much and delivered so little.

panels.description: Tight on Savitri (lean lined face, bruised cheekbone, grey-streaked low knot). Her jaw tightens.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: If you set foot in Travancore again, I will treat you as I would any invader.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: Exile.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Survival. More than your kinsman received.

panels.description: Savitri (plain white, grey-streaked low knot, bruised cheekbone) leaning forward against her bound hands, fierce.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: You are building something. I see it.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: But every house you broke, every succession you denied, every woman you sent into exile, we become stories. And stories outlast walls.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: They will remember me.

panels.description: Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold) unmoved. A Nair guard's hand on Savitri's arm (plain white, bound hands), already turning her toward the flap.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Let them. I build for the living, not the remembered.

copy.speaker: SAVITRI
copy.text: That is why you will never understand us.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Evening. Nair guards (white mundu, spears) lead Savitri, a small white figure with bound hands, away down a path west through the palms. At the very edge of the horizon, a pale band of sea haze. Smoke from the burned fields drifts across the sky and mixes with the haze. Nagoji in the foreground, seen from behind (dark topknot with grey at the temples, white coat; no turban), watching. Compose it to echo 1.5: the same rising smoke, a different fire.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I watched until she was gone from sight, this woman who had been willing to burn everything for the right to remain.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The last of the old houses had fallen.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Now came the work of making sure they could never rise again.
